evidence.ref: The warp.tracker/v1 config schema is extended in .warp/tracker.py _validate with two OPTIONAL fields carrying the eligibility model: 'agent' (the single shared Agent account the whole fleet acts as) and 'ready_statuses' (the ready-for-dev status set, module default DEFAULT_READY_STATUSES = ('Approved for dev',) when omitted); the repo routing field is the EXISTING 'field' routing mechanism (C7's validated 'WARP Repo' custom field), reused not reinvented. Validation is added INSIDE the existing _validate (no second parser): a present 'agent' must be a non-empty string and a present 'ready_statuses' must be a non-empty list of non-empty strings, else TrackerConfigError by name (fail closed by name). Both fields are optional so a routing-only PLAN-0006 config stays valid. The shipped template plugin/templates/.warp/trackers.json documents all three with example values (agent, ready_statuses, and a _routing_field_comment showing the field mechanism for 'WARP Repo').

selftest (scripts/selftest.py, eligibility triple block ~4043-4098) asserts the loader rejects a blank agent and a non-list ready_statuses by name (fail closed), that a routing-only config with neither field stays valid (backward compatible), and that the omitted ready_statuses defaults to include 'Approved for dev'. The template is validated by _validate in-build (json.load + TR._validate passes).

is_eligible(ticket, config) is a pure, side-effect-free function in .warp/tracker.py alongside resolve_repo. It returns Eligibility(True, <repo id>) ONLY when all three legs hold: assignee == the single configured Agent user AND status in the ready set (config 'ready_statuses' or DEFAULT_READY_STATUSES) AND resolve_repo (the reused WARP-0601 resolver) returns exactly one known repo, reporting that repo so the caller resolves once. It FAILS CLOSED to Eligibility(False, None) on every leg - a non-dict ticket, an empty config, an unconfigured Agent, an unassigned/non-string/non-Agent assignee, a missing/non-ready status, and a missing/unknown/ambiguous repo signal (resolve_repo's TrackerRoutingError is caught, never propagated). It reads the vendor-neutral item shape (scalar assignee, scalar status, and the routing signal resolve_repo reads), not a Jira-specific one, and never guesses a repo.

selftest (~4043-4098) drives is_eligible over fake tickets: the good triple returns eligible with repo 'repo-a'; wrong-assignee, absent-assignee, non-ready-status, unresolvable-repo, and absent-routing-signal each return ineligible; a non-dict ticket (None and a str) fails closed without raising; and an unconfigured Agent fails closed.

selftest enforces the triple with teeth: a fully eligible fake ticket is eligible AND reports its repo; three negatives each flip EXACTLY ONE leg (wrong/absent assignee, a non-ready status, an unresolvable repo tag) and assert ineligible; a purity assertion snapshots the config and ticket as sorted JSON before and after a call and asserts both unchanged; and an explicit non-tautology assertion shows the full triple accepts while dropping any one leg refuses, so no leg can pass vacuously. All in scripts/selftest.py (~4043-4098), matching the file's expect() naming/registration convention; run count 1388 passed, 0 failed.
